description: Domestic architectural guidelines rooted in the principle of Ahimsa (non-violence to all life forms), strict kitchen hygiene, daytime illumination (Chauvihar), and ritual domestic purity.
schools_note: Practiced across both Digambara and Shvetambara Jain households. Highly prioritized in western India (Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra).

rules.rationale: Ahimsa and Chauvihar: Preparation and consumption of food must occur during daylight hours; abundant natural sunlight prevents microscopic insects and mold from contaminating meals.
rules.source: Acharya Hemachandra, 'Yoga Shastra', Ch. 3 (Ahimsa and Shravaka Dharma)

rules.rationale: Shaucha (Absolute Purity): Kitchen and dining areas must never share a wall, door, or plumbing service shaft with a toilet or wastewater conduit.
rules.source: Jain Shravaka-Achara Codes of Conduct (Purity Ordinances)

rules.rationale: Dining while facing East towards morning sunlight promotes pure digestion and mindful eating (Sattvic lifestyle).
rules.source: Traditional Jain Shravaka household guidance compendium

rules.rationale: Jal-Shuddhi: Underground and overhead potable water storage must be sealed, accessible for routine cleaning, completely sun-shielded to avoid algae/larvae, and distanced from sewage lines.
rules.source: Jain Dharma Prakasha (Water Purity and An-Chhana Pani prohibitions)

rules.rationale: Grain, pulse, and dry grocery store (Bhandar) must remain elevated, well-ventilated, and completely moisture-free to prevent weevil/insect emergence.
rules.source: Traditional Shravaka household kitchen and storage management manuals

rules.rationale: Derasar / home temple must be in the pristine Ishanya zone; placing an altar directly below a second-floor bathroom or wastewater pipe is strictly forbidden.
rules.source: Vastu Vidhan for Jinalayas and Griha-Chaityas

rules.rationale: Continuous airflow and daylight dispel darkness, dampness, and insect infestation throughout the domestic dwelling.
rules.source: Ratnakaranda Shravakachara (Moral living and residential purity)

rules.rationale: Open roof terrace designed with rapid slope drainage to avoid water stagnancy (breeding ground for mosquitoes).
rules.source: Traditional sanitary guidelines for Jain urban dwellings
